title: perf(kitty): speak the rc protocol on the socket directly instead of a kitten @ client per call
description:
## .what

where a skill queries or drives kitty, talk to kitty's remote-control socket directly with the documented protocol, instead of a fresh `kitten @ <cmd>` client per call.

## .why

- measured upstream in kovidgoyal/kitty#3209: `kitty @ ls` takes **~77ms**, and the kitty maintainer states that is almost entirely client startup time; a direct socket roundtrip with the documented protocol takes **~10-20ms**
- measured on a dev box: a 10s churn sample saw **~114 distinct short-lived `kitten` processes** and ~57 `kitty` processes, steady across samples (clock-driven, not workload)
- the protocol is documented (kitty remote-control protocol): a JSON `kitty-cmd` payload framed as an escape sequence, sent over the `listen_on` unix socket

## .proposed shape

- one small socket client (or a resident helper) that speaks the rc protocol, used by the termwork / duct skills that today call `kitten @ ls`, `@ send-text`, and similar on a loop
- for state a loop re-reads (e.g. the window list), prefer a cache refreshed on change over a query per tick

## .acceptance

- the hot paths that call `kitten @` on a loop use the direct socket client
- measured before/after: distinct `kitten` processes per 10s sample, and the per-call latency

## .sources

- https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/issues/3209
- https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/rc_protocol/
- https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/remote-control/
